title: Can the Top Lawyer Be Fair? Senators Ask Tough Questions
summary: Have you ever had to be fair to someone you didn't get along with? That's the huge challenge facing Todd Blanche right now. He used to be President Trump's personal lawyer—like a legal bodyguard. Now he wants to be the top lawyer for the entire country, leading the Department of Justice (DOJ). The DOJ is like the nation's biggest law firm; it makes sure laws are followed and keeps everyone safe. But here's the twist: lots of senators are worried Blanche might still act like the president's personal lawyer, not a fair referee for all Americans. On Wednesday, July 15, 2026, Blanche sat before the Senate Judiciary Committee. That's a group of senators who check if he's right for the job. They grilled him with questions for two days. The biggest worry? Loyalty. Blanche once defended Trump in a New York trial where Trump was found guilty of 34 crimes for faking business records. Now, as acting attorney general, Blanche has already made moves that make people wonder. For example, in May 2026, he approved a settlement that shields Trump and his family from future tax investigations by the IRS. Critics say that looks like protecting a friend, not serving justice. Blanche says he's fixing a DOJ that was "weaponized"—used unfairly—against Trump before. He points to good news: violent crime dropped in 2025, and the DOJ is fighting drug cartels. "I'm proud of what we've done to help American families see safer streets," he told the senators. Still, many worry the DOJ might go after Trump's political rivals, like former FBI director James Comey. The big question remains: can Blanche be independent? The Senate hasn't decided yet. It's a tense moment that could shape how fair our laws really are.
why_it_matters: If the person in charge of making sure everyone follows the rules can't be fair, it's like having a referee who always favors one team—the whole game, and the whole country, would feel it's not just.

background_read: The Department of Justice (DOJ) is the nation's top law enforcement agency, and the attorney general is its boss. Normally, the president picks someone and the Senate must vote to confirm them.
In 2024, Donald Trump was found guilty of 34 felonies for fake business records, and Todd Blanche was one of his main defense lawyers in that trial.
The Senate Judiciary Committee holds hearings where senators grill nominees to decide if they should be allowed to hold such a powerful job.
Article_Structure: WHO: Todd Blanche, President Donald Trump, the Senate Judiciary Committee, and former FBI director James Comey
WHAT: Blanche faced tough questions from senators about whether he can be independent, since he used to be Trump's personal lawyer and has already made moves that seem to protect Trump
WHERE: A Senate Judiciary Committee hearing room on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.
WHY: The Senate must decide if Blanche is right to lead the DOJ fairly for all Americans, not just to help the president who was once his client

perspectives.description: They say he is fixing a broken system that was unfairly used against Trump, and point to lower crime rates as proof he is doing a good job.
They see the IRS settlement as a favor to a friend, and fear the DOJ under Blanche might attack Trump's enemies instead of treating everyone equally.
Many just want to be sure that the laws apply the same to powerful people and regular people, and that decisions are not made to help old friends.
